text:
ava: FYI hitting a provisioning bottleneck in us-west-2 — ENI attach rate limits + node group hitting quota. GPU pods Pending ~280, most are batch-job-sweep replicas. :warning:
liam: ugh. any obvious hot cron?
sanjay: looks like cron-sweep-04 scaled to 200 replicas due to failed retries, controllers kept requeueing. that plus a few large finetune jobs.
ava: confirmed, controller history shows repeated crashloop -> restart bursts. autoscaler started scale-up, cloud provider reports ENI_ATTACH_THROTTLEDs. new instances stuck in provisioning for 6-12m.
ops-bot: [alert] EC2 API throttling: DescribeNetworkInterfaces throttled  (region=us-west-2)
maria: can we temporarily move batch-sweep to a lower priority QoS or nodeSelector to avoid GPU pool?
liam: suggest two-prong: 1) emergency eviction of low-priority batch pods; 2) manual nodegroup increase with different instance family (p4 -> g5) to avoid ENI constraints.
sanjay: ENI attach is per-AZ and per-instance-type. switching instance family helps but SKU availability might block. also cost will spike.
oncall-rohit: I'm on it, doing a quick triage. first step: mark nodegroup autoscaling disabled for GPU-ng-1 to stop the autoscaler loop spamming API.
ava: good. set CA flags to avoid repeated attempts: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and throttle scale-up? maybe increase `--max-node-provision-time=15m`.
kube-autoscaler-bot: detected scale-up loop: attempted scale-up x12 in last 8m, failed due to provider errors.
liam: manual mitigation executed: increasing GPU-fallback-ng by +6 nodes of g5.2xlarge, will be billed as on-demand. starting at t+2m.
sanjay: also deploying a cluster-level PDB and adding a temporary taint `reserved=batch-pause:NoSchedule` to prevent new batch pods from binding to GPU nodes.
maria: evicting low-priority pods now with: `kubectl delete pods -l job=batch-sweep,priority=low --grace-period=0 --force` — started drain.
oncall-rohit: ENI errors dropping from 6xx to 2xx after throttling window; seeing attaches succeed now for the fallback group. new nodes are registering.
ava: good progress. timeline: pending dropped from 280 -> 80 over 7m. still some long-waits for large finetune jobs.
liam: we should patch scheduler to prefer node affinity for finetune jobs so they don't backfill onto scarce ENI hosttypes. longer term: consider enabling CNI trunking or ENI quotas bump with AWS.
sanjay: filed request to cloud with support ticket #CS-92441 for ENI quota increase in two AZs. added notes about burst patterns.
maria: cost note: fallback will add ~+$9k/day while on-demand. we need PO approval if persists beyond 24h.
ava: for immediate stability, switching batch-sweep to run at 0300 UTC and rate-limiting controllers to prevent scale bursts. patch pushed to cron controller to cap replica bursts to 30.
kube-autoscaler-bot: scale-up cooldown in effect until 2318766000. next automated attempt scheduled at 2318766200.
oncall-rohit: follow-ups: 1) revert taints after stabilization; 2) confirm ticket CS-92441 progress; 3) coordinate with cost for emergency PO. I'm staying on pager.
liam: logging note: captured `aws ec2 AttachNetworkInterface` errors in cloudtrail — saving for postmortem.
sanjay: postmortem action items draft: - ENI quota monitoring alert - policy to fallback instance families automatically - limit cron replica spikes - add preemptible-only nodepool for batch 
maria: adding cost guardrails: auto-approve up to $2k/day for emergency, beyond that require finance ack.
ava: final state update: cluster stable, pending down to 7, fallback nodes healthy. rolling back cron cap after one maintenance window. will keep ENI ticket open. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
liam: nice containment. leaving notes for runbook updates.
oncall-rohit: closing incident channel soon, will open a follow-up thread for postmortem draft.
ops-bot: [info] Incident tagged: gpu-provisioning-eniname-pressure, severity=sev2
